_comment: The node event: routing is one board event that names the node that reacts.
`task:handoff` on cadre/tasks carries `node` — the specialist that takes the
work next. ONE action starts whichever node the event names; the name is
read from the event (`{payload[node]}`), never written into the action. So
adding a specialist is registering it, with `command:task:handoff` in its
`reads`: it then appears on every page's verdict form and in every node's
prompt (runnerlib/tasks.handoff_nodes), and this action starts it. No new
action, no daemon restart — the registry is re-read every pass.
Who writes the event: the driver, by picking a node on a page's verdict
form (the surface bridge), or an agent handing off itself
(`pipeline.py handoff`). Both go through runnerlib/tasks.write_handoff, which
refuses a node that is not registered to take a handoff before anything is
written. An event that names such a node anyway (written some other way)
fails here as a failed firing and a `signal: failed` on the task's key.
What happens after the node reacts is not decided here. Its page offers
the next handoff the same way; which nodes connect is which nodes listen.
Continue on a page goes back through the node that built it: that is the
feedback action in config/actions-dialogue.json, generic the same way.

actions.name: task-handed-to-a-node
actions._why: the node event: start whichever registered node it names, in the task's directory, with the page it was handed from as its input and the annotations as its last instructions
